newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin says against more privatisations.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin says against more privatisations.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin said on Tuesday he was against continuing privatisations and said a Socialist government would not sell France Telecom.
"We are not in favour of continuing privatisations" he said in a television interview. "We will not carry out the privatisation of France Telecom," he said.
The ruling centre-right coalition has pledged to press ahead with privatisations if it wins an early two-round parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.
But it said on Tuesday it would delay by four weeks, to June 6, the launch of the sale of a minority stake in France Telecom to avoid a clash with the election.
It has also pledged to press ahead with the sale of defence electronics group Thomson CSF. But Jospin said that "if Thomson is to be sold for one franc, honestly that is not what we want to do."

No opinion polls have been released since French President Jacques Chirac announced an early election on Monday. And although financial markets generally expect the centre-right to win, some economists are warning the result could be very close.
